title: Meronic Structural Foundations
deck:
Meronic Structural Foundations organize outward cuboctahedral growth
            through free Alpha Triads, with validated cumulative totals through
            the Fifth Foundation.

concise.body:
Merons

The following "tridirectional" (3D) images and animations show the growth mode and the true forms of organization of the Meronic structures, from the internal structure of the Metalpha Merons (hydrogen), whose spatial arrangement of the 12 Alpha Points of its 12 Compalphas form the structure of a cuboctahedron, passing through the Dodecalpha Meron (carbon 12), with 12 cuboctahedra, continuing beyond the validated Fifth Foundation toward a type of Meron whose number of Cuboctahedra and their Structural Dimension are undefined.

The fundamental components of the Meron Metalpha structure, which are its 12 Compalphas, when connected by their Alpha Points, form a cuboctahedral geometric solid, as we see in the 2nd animation.

When filling out these Structural Foundations, each Cuboctahedron, which is formed by a set of 12 Compalphas, is only connected to, at most, 4 other Cuboctahedra, through 4 of its 8 triangular faces, which are made up of 4 Alpha Triads.

But as there is an imposition of the Rotating Interaction rule, which requires that all infinite Interaction Circles be in "rotational synchronism", each of these first 4 cuboctahedra is only immediately connected to another cuboctahedron, called the "internal connection" cuboctahedron.

The successive connections of cuboctahedra provide a Meronic growth factor depending on the maximum number of cuboctahedra in a given layer external to the forming Meron.

Fcm = (ni.1) + (ne.3), where

Fcm = Meronic growth factor.

ni = The number of Internal Bond Cuboctahedra

ne = The number of External Link Cuboctahedra.

These "external connection" cuboctahedra are linked to other cuboctahedra, however, starting from the fourth Structural Foundation, some of these cuboctahedra are also common to the previous Foundation, forming fractions of cuboctahedra in multiplications.

1st - First Meronic Structural Foundation

The First Foundation (1F) contains, at most, 1 Cuboctahedron, 1F = 1, totaling a Meron with 1 Cuboctahedron. And this chemical element is Meron Metalpha, whose structure is formed by 12 Compalphas, known as hydrogen.

We must understand that animations 5.4.1 and 5.4.2 represent the same structure, which is Meron Metalpha.

2nd - Second Meronic Structural Foundation

The Second Foundation (2F) allows, at most, 4 Cuboctahedra, 2F = 4. Because the first Cuboctahedron (Metalpha) only allows, at most, 4 connections, thus, Fcm = (0. 1) + (0. 3) = 4, forming a Meron with 5 Cuboctahedra, which results from the sum of 1F1 + 2F4, and which is the Pentalpha Meron (helium 5).

The next Meron will be the result of the multiplication of the 4 External Link Cuboctahedra of the Pentalpha Meron, which allow connection with 4 others, one Internal Link Cuboctahedron, and another 3 External Link Cuboctahedra. Thus, the Third Structural Foundation will be the result of the multiplication of these last cuboctahedra of the Second Foundation, so, Fcm = (4.

3rd - Third Meronic Structural Foundation

The Third Foundation (3F) contains, at most, 16 cuboctahedra, 3F = 16, which results from Fcm = (4. 1) + (4. 3) = 16, and which added to the cuboctahedra of foundation 1F and 2F (1F1 + 2F4 + 3F16), form a Meron with 21 Cuboctahedra, which we can also say is the "number of mass" of the Meron Heneicosalpha, better known as the "Neon atom".

So that between the closure of the 2nd and 3rd Structural Foundation we have a "structural equivalent" of 16 "energy levels", where each new cuboctahedron added is characterized as the new Meron type, with different "physical-chemical" properties.

4th - Fourth Meronic Structural Foundation

The Fourth Foundation (4F) holds, at most, 48 Cuboctahedra, 4F = 48, totaling a Meron with 69 Cuboctahedra, (21+48) or the sum of 1F1..., 4F48. For the next multiplier, the formula does not work if it is not taken into account that some Cuboctahedra are shared among the Foundations, so, by counting in the virtual model, we can see that they are Fcm = (12. 4) + (24. 1.5) = 84 (or Fcm = (12.4) + (12.3) = 84).

So that between the closure of the 3rd and 4th Structural Foundations we have a "structural equivalent" of 48 "energy levels", where each new Cuboctahedron added is characterized as the new Meron type, with different "chemical" properties.

5th - Fifth Meronic Structural Foundation

The Fifth Foundation (5F) holds, at most, 84 Cuboctahedra, 5F = 84, result of (12. 4) + (24. 1.5) = 84, totaling a Meron with 153 Cuboctahedra, (69+84) or the sum of 1F1..., 5F84.

So that between the closure of the 4th and 5th Structural Foundations we have a "structural equivalent" of 84 "energy levels", where each new Cuboctahedron added is characterized as the new Meron type, with different "physiochemical" properties.

Foundations beyond 5F remain under geometric review.

Natural Structural Deconstruction (natural decay)

Natural structural deconstruction (natural decay) may affect very large Meronic structures when the geometric density and pressure of their Interaction Circles become insufficient outside stellar cores.

5.6 The Meronic Structural Quadrants

As for the order of distribution of the cuboctahedra in the Meron structure, what we can do, since there are no such "energy levels" occupied by supposed "fundamental particles", there are no such "quantum numbers", is to divide the Meron structure into spatial quadrants.

So we will have 8 quadrants (of Cartesian space), where each new cuboctahedron, added to its structure, will have its own set of coordinates, as we can see in the animation alongside.

So that each cuboctahedron in Quadrant Q1 will have a symmetric cuboctahedron in Quadrant Q3, the cuboctahedra in Quadrant Q2 will have symmetric cuboctahedra in Quadrant Q4, those in Quadrant Q5 will have their symmetric ones in Quadrant Q7, and the cuboctahedra in Quadrant Q6 in Quadrant Q8, like images in a mirror.

Now, as for the number of connections that each type of Meron is capable of making with other Merons, it only depends on the relationship between the types of Merons and the number of Structural Foundations they have.

According to TUIDG, the abundance or scarcity of certain types of Merons is due to two factors: 1st, the predominant energy level in each "region" of space, or in each quadrant dominated by a star;

The higher the energy level of a region of space, such as within stars or galactic centers, the larger and more abundant Merons will be in that region. The transformation of supposed neutrons into supposed protons is a phenomenon that physicists say is widely observed in nuclear fission processes or the natural decay of radio isotopes.

According to TUIDG, the concept of energy is not that of a dynamic of indefinite fragmentation of matter, according to its guidelines, what they call energy is, simply, an Apparent Motion of vibration or oscillation of the mesh of the Geometric Continuum, which can only exist in the structure of the Geometric Hypercontinuum.

The Pentacontahexalpha Meron (Meron 56 or Ferri 56) Tridirectional view of the Hentetracontahectalpha Meron (Meron 141), formed by 141 Cuboctahedra, Foundation 5F 141,..

5.7.14 A fragment of a Star Crystal

What we have here is an assumption, a conjecture, about the possibility of there being a type of fragments resulting from the breakage of a Stellar Crystal, that is, an enormous Meron formed by a very large number of Cuboctahedra.

full.body:
Merons

The following "tridirectional" (3D) images and animations show the growth mode and the true forms of organization of the Meronic structures, from the internal structure of the Metalpha Merons (hydrogen), whose spatial arrangement of the 12 Alpha Points of its 12 Compalphas form the structure of a cuboctahedron, passing through the Dodecalpha Meron (carbon 12), with 12 cuboctahedra, continuing beyond the validated Fifth Foundation toward a type of Meron whose number of Cuboctahedra and their Structural Dimension are undefined.

The fundamental components of the Meron Metalpha structure, which are its 12 Compalphas, when connected by their Alpha Points, form a cuboctahedral geometric solid, as we see in the 2nd animation. Thus, all types of Merons can also be represented, both with their "almost real" structure, seen with their Interaction Circles, and in their simplified form, formed only by their Cuboctahedra. In the 1st animation we have the "tridirectional" (3D) representation of the Meron Metalpha, as "secondary building blocks" of all existing types of Merons (atoms), since the "primary blocks" are their Compalphas.

The growth of the Meronic structure does not occur through a supposed enormous number of "fundamental particles", with their illogical mechanisms based on "random throws" (exchanges), with supposed "quantized energy levels". The supposed "fundamental particles" of physicists, according to TUIDG's description, are just the various aspects of a single absolutely geometric structure called the Alpha Component or Compalpha, and there is, therefore, no supposed form of "corpuscular energy", but only a quantity of "oscillation/vibration" of the Alpha Axes of these Compalphas, which are the structural components of all Merons.

So we don't have a "matter structure" and an "energy structure" as two distinct and interchangeable characteristics, but just a type of "geometric structure" that is, at the same time, "matter" and "energy", as something inseparable, nothing like "particles" loose in space "hitting" each other back and forth. So it is these "secondary blocks", in the form of cuboctahedra, that form all types of existing Merons. These units are appropriately arranged in space, depending on their shapes, in terms of what we can call "structural layers" or Structural Foundations.

When filling out these Structural Foundations, each Cuboctahedron, which is formed by a set of 12 Compalphas, is only connected to, at most, 4 other Cuboctahedra, through 4 of its 8 triangular faces, which are made up of 4 Alpha Triads. So that the Cuboctahedron of the 1st (initial) foundation admits connection with the first 4 Cuboctahedra, forming a Meron with up to 5 Cuboctahedra, which is the Meron Pentalpha (helium 5), with a central Cuboctahedron and 4 external ones. Thus, as each of these 4 external cuboctahedra already connects to the central cuboctahedron, by this rule, they can now only connect to the other 3.

But as there is an imposition of the Rotating Interaction rule, which requires that all infinite Interaction Circles be in "rotational synchronism", each of these first 4 cuboctahedra is only immediately connected to another cuboctahedron, called the "internal connection" cuboctahedron. And this cuboctahedron is what connects to 3 other "external connection" cuboctahedra. These "external connection" Cuboctahedra, for the same reason, only connect to 3 other "internal connection" Cuboctahedra, and so on.

The Meronic Structural Foundations

In the current construction rule, every new Cuboctahedron grows outward through one of the three free outer Alpha Triads of the preceding unit. A new unit never grows inward through a previous Meronic layer.

The successive connections of cuboctahedra provide a Meronic growth factor depending on the maximum number of cuboctahedra in a given layer external to the forming Meron. And a preliminary, very rough formula might be like the following:

Fcm = (ni.1) + (ne.3), where

Fcm = Meronic growth factor.

ni = The number of Internal Bond Cuboctahedra

ne = The number of External Link Cuboctahedra.

These "external connection" cuboctahedra are linked to other cuboctahedra, however, starting from the fourth Structural Foundation, some of these cuboctahedra are also common to the previous Foundation, forming fractions of cuboctahedra in multiplications.

Animation 5.4.1 - The Meron Metalpha, the simplest Meron

1st - First Meronic Structural Foundation

The First Foundation (1F) contains, at most, 1 Cuboctahedron, 1F = 1, totaling a Meron with 1 Cuboctahedron. And this chemical element is Meron Metalpha, whose structure is formed by 12 Compalphas, known as hydrogen.

We must understand that animations 5.4.1 and 5.4.2 represent the same structure, which is Meron Metalpha. The first is its "almost real" aspect, seen with its Interaction Circles, and the second is its extremely simplified form, formed only by the cuboctahedron that results from the connection between the 12 Alpha Points of its 12 Compalphas.

The type of Rotating Interaction that predominates in this, as well as in all Meronic structures, is the Meronic-Intrameronic Interaction, promoted by the Meronic Circles, fundamentally "attractive", and the Intrameronic Circles, fundamentally "repulsive". The intensity of the "attraction/repulsion" forces of these first two Interaction Circles are the logical equivalents of the illogical "strong force", which would be the product of the "exchange" of supposed "gluons" between supposed "quarks".

Animation 5.4.2 - The Meron Metalpha, Cuboctahedral form

2nd - Second Meronic Structural Foundation

The Second Foundation (2F) allows, at most, 4 Cuboctahedra, 2F = 4. Because the first Cuboctahedron (Metalpha) only allows, at most, 4 connections, thus, Fcm = (0. 1) + (0. 3) = 4, forming a Meron with 5 Cuboctahedra, which results from the sum of 1F1 + 2F4, and which is the Pentalpha Meron (helium 5).

The next Meron will be the result of the multiplication of the 4 External Link Cuboctahedra of the Pentalpha Meron, which allow connection with 4 others, one Internal Link Cuboctahedron, and another 3 External Link Cuboctahedra. Thus, the Third Structural Foundation will be the result of the multiplication of these last cuboctahedra of the Second Foundation, so, Fcm = (4. 1) + (4. 3) = 16.

Animation 5.4.3 - The Meron Pentalpha, Cuboctahedral shape

3rd - Third Meronic Structural Foundation

The Third Foundation (3F) contains, at most, 16 cuboctahedra, 3F = 16, which results from Fcm = (4. 1) + (4. 3) = 16, and which added to the cuboctahedra of foundation 1F and 2F (1F1 + 2F4 + 3F16), form a Meron with 21 Cuboctahedra, which we can also say is the "number of mass" of the Meron Heneicosalpha, better known as the "Neon atom".

So that between the closure of the 2nd and 3rd Structural Foundation we have a "structural equivalent" of 16 "energy levels", where each new cuboctahedron added is characterized as the new Meron type, with different "physical-chemical" properties. And this has nothing to do with filling supposed "s, p, d, f" orbitals with supposed "electrons".

Animation 5.4.4 - Meron 21 closes the third Structural Foundation

4th - Fourth Meronic Structural Foundation

The Fourth Foundation (4F) holds, at most, 48 Cuboctahedra, 4F = 48, totaling a Meron with 69 Cuboctahedra, (21+48) or the sum of 1F1..., 4F48. For the next multiplier, the formula does not work if it is not taken into account that some Cuboctahedra are shared among the Foundations, so, by counting in the virtual model, we can see that they are Fcm = (12. 4) + (24. 1.5) = 84 (or Fcm = (12.4) + (12.3) = 84).

So that between the closure of the 3rd and 4th Structural Foundations we have a "structural equivalent" of 48 "energy levels", where each new Cuboctahedron added is characterized as the new Meron type, with different "chemical" properties.

Animation 5.4.5 - Meron 69 closes the fourth Structural Foundation

5th - Fifth Meronic Structural Foundation

The Fifth Foundation (5F) holds, at most, 84 Cuboctahedra, 5F = 84, result of (12. 4) + (24. 1.5) = 84, totaling a Meron with 153 Cuboctahedra, (69+84) or the sum of 1F1..., 5F84.

So that between the closure of the 4th and 5th Structural Foundations we have a "structural equivalent" of 84 "energy levels", where each new Cuboctahedron added is characterized as the new Meron type, with different "physiochemical" properties.

Animation 5.4.6 - Meron 153 closes the fifth Structural Foundation

Foundations beyond 5F remain under geometric review. The historical 6F and 7F counts and their derived totals are not reproduced as validated results in this edition.

Natural Structural Deconstruction (natural decay)

Natural structural deconstruction (natural decay) may affect very large Meronic structures when the geometric density and pressure of their Interaction Circles become insufficient outside stellar cores. Foundation counts beyond 5F remain under review.

5.6 The Meronic Structural Quadrants

As for the order of distribution of the cuboctahedra in the Meron structure, what we can do, since there are no such "energy levels" occupied by supposed "fundamental particles", there are no such "quantum numbers", is to divide the Meron structure into spatial quadrants.

So we will have 8 quadrants (of Cartesian space), where each new cuboctahedron, added to its structure, will have its own set of coordinates, as we can see in the animation alongside. Knowledge about this mode of "cuboctahedral organization" will have several practical purposes when we are able to "construct" any type of Meron cuboctahedron by cuboctahedron.

Animation 5.6.1 - The Meronic Quadrants

This "Meronic mapping" is equivalent, in quantitative terms, to such "quantum levels", but with practical functionality, and without all its absurdities. Thus, we will have the following quadrants, Q1 = (x,y,z), Q2 = (-x,y,z), Q3 = (-x,y,-z), Q4 = (z,y,-z), Q5 = (x,-y,z), Q6 = (-x,-y,z), Q7 = (-x,-y,-z) and Q8 = (x,-y,-z), where the cuboctahedra occupy "positive" or "negatives along the x, y and z spatial axes.

So that each cuboctahedron in Quadrant Q1 will have a symmetric cuboctahedron in Quadrant Q3, the cuboctahedra in Quadrant Q2 will have symmetric cuboctahedra in Quadrant Q4, those in Quadrant Q5 will have their symmetric ones in Quadrant Q7, and the cuboctahedra in Quadrant Q6 in Quadrant Q8, like images in a mirror.

Maybe nature doesn't make the decision to fill quadrants for pure pleasure, but it seems logical, at least from the point of view of dynamic equilibrium, that the growth mode is like this. So, for example, be the case of the transition from the Hexalpha Meron to the Heptalpha Meron, where the new cuboctahedron is added in an opposite quadrant of this Meron, and not in an adjacent one, precisely in the position of a dynamic balance resulting from a possible rotation of the Meron.

Now, as for the number of connections that each type of Meron is capable of making with other Merons, it only depends on the relationship between the types of Merons and the number of Structural Foundations they have. Probably somewhere between 4 and 16 (perhaps even 32) bonds, something very far from the determinations of traditional chemistry. 5.7 The first 12 Merons and the Stellar Crystal

5.7.1 Metalpha (Hydrogen 1), the first Meron

Tridirectional (3D) view of the Meron Metalpha (hydrogen 1), which is made up of twelve Compalphas, and which only has one structural form. According to traditional chemistry, the most common isotope of hydrogen does not have neutrons, there are two others, deuterium (D), with one neutron, and tritium (T), radioactive, with two. Deuterium has a natural abundance of between 0.0184 and 0.0082% (IUPAC), many times lower than that of isotope 1, which reaches more than 98% of the total mass of everything we can perceive in the apparent universe.

According to TUIDG, the abundance or scarcity of certain types of Merons is due to two factors: 1st, the predominant energy level in each "region" of space, or in each quadrant dominated by a star; 2nd, to the types of pre-existing forms of Merons in these quadrants.

The higher the energy level of a region of space, such as within stars or galactic centers, the larger and more abundant Merons will be in that region. It is noted that the largest and most stable Meron existing in the observable universe, such as the Meron Hectanonaetalpha (Iridium 192), the Meron Pentacontahexalpha (Iron 56), and the Meron Pentacontaoctalpha (Cobalt 58), are only formed in the cores of stars, mainly at the end of their lives.

And these are only stored in distant bodies, such as comets and asteroids, as a result of the formation of remnants of these stellar explosions. The smallest and most abundant Meron, Metalpha (Hydrogen 1), is found throughout interplanetary and interstellar space, since these regions are low in energy compared to stellar or galactic cores. What happens in these two situations is, firstly, a process of Meronic composition and, in the second situation, a natural decomposition of more complex, more unstable structures, until a less complex or more stable structure. It is, simply, a natural decay of structures, through a decrease in the level of "energy" predominant in each region of space.

Animation 6.4.1 - The Meron Metalpha (left), view of the cuboctahedron formed by the 12 Alpha Points and the view of its "fields" (right)

In animation 5.7.1 above, only the vertices, edges and sides of Meron Metalpha are being shown, that is, without the full range of interaction circles they actually have. It is the representation at the level of the Octahedral Cube structure of "hydrogen", in its most abundant and stable form. And in the animation below, we can see what the first two types of Interaction Circles look like, the Intrameronic Circles (in white), in a mode of mutual repulsion of the structure itself, and the Meronic Circles (in blue), in an attraction mode.

The interaction mechanism is like this: As the Meronic Circles tend to collapse the Meron structure, bringing the Alpha Points closer indefinitely, as they are intrinsically attractive, the Intrameronic Circles, which are intrinsically repulsive, counterbalance this collapse with the same intensity. They also repel, in the same way, the Intrameronic circles of the other Merons, more precisely, the circles of individual cuboctahedra, in the process of Meronic formation or growth.

5.7.2 The Metalpha Merons and the supposed Protons and Neutrons

The transformation of supposed neutrons into supposed protons is a phenomenon that physicists say is widely observed in nuclear fission processes or the natural decay of radio isotopes. According to traditional atomic physics, in this process there is a release of energy and, as neutrons are more massive than protons, they lose part of their mass and, consequently, undergo transmutation into protons, as energy is matter in motion. According to TUIDG, there really is a transformation of structures, however, not of protons into neutrons.

According to TUIDG, the concept of energy is not that of a dynamic of indefinite fragmentation of matter, according to its guidelines, what they call energy is, simply, an Apparent Motion of vibration or oscillation of the mesh of the Geometric Continuum, which can only exist in the structure of the Geometric Hypercontinuum. In this structure, a Compalpha, and in this case a Cuboctahedron or Metalpha expelled from any Meron, has a very intense apparent rotation, and when passing through other types of Merons or among their similar ones (in the original structure or outside it), it does not interact geometrically until it loses part of this rotation and is geometrically absorbed by these target structures or causes a structural dissociation in that same structure. In the previous Three-Directional (3D) animation, we can see what could be mistakenly called the dual aspect of Compalpha, that is, the proton and neutron aspects.

5.7.3 Etalpha (Hydrogen 2 or Deuterium), the second Meron

Tridirectional (3D) view of the Meron Etalpha (Hydrogen 2 or Deuterium), formed by two Cuboctahedra, Foundation 2F 1, which are made up of 21 Compalphas and which do not present structural heteromorphism. The number of Compalphas that constitute it is not equal to 24, because at the junction between the two Cuboctahedra, an alpha triad (three Compalphas) ​​is common to the two Cuboctahedra of the Meronic structure, so that the count of Compalphas of the Meron can be done using the formula Nc = Ne × K + T, once the number of Cuboctahedra of the structure is known, with K = 9 and T = 3 (Ne = Structural number, Nc = Component number and T = Common Triad of the Interaction).

Animation 5.7.3 - A Meron Etalpha (Deuterium), seen in its metacubic form (on the left) and in its "field" form (on the right)

5.7.4 Propalpha (Hydrogen 3 or Tritium), the third Meron

Tridirectional (3D) view of the Meron Propalpha (Hydrogen 3 or Tritium), formed by three Cuboctahedra, Foundation 2F 2, which are made up of 30 Compalphas. It can present structural heteromorphism with two distinct forms. It is, together with Meron Heptalpha and Dodecalpha, one of the most important elements for the construction process of the different types of existing Merons.

Its importance is due to the fact that it can be easily fitted into any type of existing Meron, promoting Meronic construction or deconstruction. Perhaps it is due to its ease in interacting naturally that it is a practically non-existent element under moderate conditions of temperature and pressure.

According to the description of traditional chemistry, it is an isotope of hydrogen, and the least abundant, it contains one proton and two neutrons (mass 3). It is a radioactive isotope that has an average lifespan of 12.3 years. As the nucleus has three nucleons that participate in the strong interaction, and only one electrically charged proton, tritium can carry out nuclear fusion more easily than the most common isotope of hydrogen.

Animation 5.7.4 - The Meron Propalpha (Tritium, from Hydrogen), vision of the cubes and vision of the "force fields".

5.7.5 Butalpha (Helios 4), the fourth Meron

Tridirectional (3D) view of the Meron Butalpha (Helium 4), formed by four Cuboctahedra, Foundation 2F 3, which are made up of 39 Compalphas. It can also present structural heteromorphism with at least two more forms.

Animation 5.7.5 - The Meron Butalpha

According to traditional description, the most common isotope of helium is He 4, whose nucleus is made up of two protons and two neutrons. Helium has a second isotope, He 3, in addition to heavier ones that are radioactive. Helium-3 is practically non-existent on Earth, as alpha decay exclusively produces helium-4 nuclei.

Its exceptional nuclear stability would be due to the fact that it would have a magic number of nucleons, that is, a quantity that is distributed in complete levels (in a similar way to how electrons are distributed in orbitals). 5.7.14 A fragment of a Star Crystal

What we have here is an assumption, a conjecture, about the possibility of there being a type of fragments resulting from the breakage of a Stellar Crystal, that is, an enormous Meron formed by a very large number of Cuboctahedra. Because, according to TUIDG, all stars have, at their core, a solid and crystalline structure whose final shape tends to be that of a gigantic cuboctahedron. So, eventually, under the force of events happening in the stellar core, these crystals could rupture, and their fragments could be left wandering around the star. In this situation, once such "fragments" are formed, they will probably tend to decompose very quickly to the point of becoming stable in conditions of temperature and pressure other than those of the stellar core, and this stability would be achieved when the structure reaches something around 266 cuboctahedra.
